title: Pas d'accord !
subtitle: Four arguments, from polite to firm
review: Written by Claude. Check the French, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: The heating, a suitcase with six pairs of shoes, some missing chocolate and pineapple on pizza: four small arguments between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how the disagreement goes from polite to firm, and how they end it.

lines.text: Il fait froid ici, non ?

tr.en: It's cold in here, isn't it?

lines.text: Je dirais pas ça. Il fait vingt-deux.

tr.en: I wouldn't say that. It's twenty-two degrees.

lines.note: = je ne dirais pas ça. Twenty-two degrees Celsius is about 72°F.

lines.text: Je suis pas tout à fait d'accord. Je porte trois pulls.

tr.en: I don't quite agree. I'm wearing three jumpers.

lines.text: Je vois ce que tu veux dire, mais le chauffage coûte cher.

tr.en: I see what you mean, but heating is expensive.

lines.text: Ça se discute. Un rhume aussi, ça coûte cher.

tr.en: That's debatable. A cold is expensive too.

lines.text: Avec tout le respect que je te dois, le troisième pull, c'est le mien.

tr.en: With all due respect, the third jumper is mine.

lines.note: A formal phrase, normally for a boss or an elder. Here it is comically pompous.

lines.text: Il traînait sur le canapé.

tr.en: It was lying around on the sofa.

lines.note: Traîner: to lie around, to be left out.

lines.text: J'étais dedans.

tr.en: I was in it.

lines.text: Six paires de chaussures ? On part deux jours.

tr.en: Six pairs of shoes? We're going away for two days.

lines.text: Pas exactement. Deux jours et demi.

tr.en: Not exactly. Two and a half days.

lines.text: Tu vas toutes les mettre ?

tr.en: Are you going to wear them all?

lines.note: Mettre: to put on, to wear.

lines.text: Je pense pas.

tr.en: I don't think so.

lines.text: Alors t'en as pas vraiment besoin.

tr.en: Then you don't really need them.

lines.note: Avoir besoin de becomes en: t'en as pas besoin.

lines.text: Oui, mais je sais pas encore lesquelles.

tr.en: Yes, but I don't know which ones yet.

lines.text: Je comprends, mais la valise ferme plus.

tr.en: I understand, but the suitcase won't close any more.

lines.note: Ferme plus = ne ferme plus: 'no longer closes', not 'closes more'.

lines.text: Je suis pas de ton avis. Assieds-toi dessus.

tr.en: I don't see it that way. Sit on it.

lines.text: C'est toi qui as fini le chocolat.

tr.en: You're the one who finished the chocolate.

lines.note: As, not a: the verb agrees with toi.

lines.text: Pas du tout !

tr.en: Not at all!

lines.text: Il en restait trois carrés hier soir.

tr.en: There were three squares left last night.

lines.text: C'est faux. Il en restait deux.

tr.en: That's not true. There were two left.

lines.text: Donc tu les as comptés.

tr.en: So you counted them.

lines.text: Ça n'a rien à voir.

tr.en: That has nothing to do with it.

lines.text: T'as du chocolat sur le menton.

tr.en: You've got chocolate on your chin.

lines.text: Tu te trompes. C'est… du café.

tr.en: You're wrong. It's… coffee.

lines.text: Je suis pas d'accord. Le café, ça sent pas la noisette.

tr.en: I disagree. Coffee doesn't smell of hazelnut.

lines.note: Sentir + a noun: to smell of.

lines.text: L'ananas sur la pizza, c'est un crime.

tr.en: Pineapple on pizza is a crime.

lines.text: Chacun son avis. Moi, j'adore.

tr.en: Each to their own. I love it.

lines.text: C'est un fruit ! Sur une pizza !

tr.en: It's a fruit! On a pizza!

lines.text: La tomate aussi, c'est un fruit.

tr.en: Tomato is a fruit too.

lines.text: Là, je te suis pas.

tr.en: I'm not with you there.

lines.note: Suivre: to follow. Je te suis pas = je ne te suis pas.

lines.text: Bon. On est pas d'accord, c'est tout.

tr.en: Right. We just don't agree, that's all.

lines.text: T'as raison, on va pas se disputer pour ça. Je peux goûter ?

tr.en: You're right, let's not fight over it. Can I have a taste?

lines.text: L'ananas ?

tr.en: The pineapple?

lines.text: Juste pour vérifier.

tr.en: Just to check.

notes: Polite: je dirais pas ça, je suis pas tout à fait d'accord, ça se discute. They keep the discussion friendly.
Oui, mais… and je comprends, mais… grant the point, then object.
Firm: pas du tout, c'est faux, tu te trompes, je suis pas d'accord. Use them with people you know well.
Ça n'a rien à voir rejects an argument as beside the point.
To end it: chacun son avis; on est pas d'accord, c'est tout; on va pas se disputer pour ça.
Spoken French drops ne: je dirais pas, je pense pas, ferme plus. In writing: je ne dirais pas, je ne pense pas, ne ferme plus.

questions.q: Lucas disagrees politely that it is cold. What does he say?
questions.why: Je dirais pas ça = 'I wouldn't say that': a gentle correction.

questions.q: Emma grants Lucas's point about the shoes, then objects. How does she begin?
questions.why: Oui, mais… accepts the point and adds the objection.

questions.q: Lucas says that counting the chocolate is beside the point. What does he say?
questions.why: Ça n'a rien à voir = 'that has nothing to do with it'.

questions.q: Emma ends the pizza argument without giving in. What does she say?
options: On est pas d'accord, c'est tout.
questions.why: On est pas d'accord, c'est tout = 'we just don't agree, that's all'.
